summary: A standard method of encapsulating 802.2 packets on networks that support Novell's IPX protocol. It obsoletes earlier documents on carrying Internet packets over IPX, and allows multiple network protocols to be carried.

eli5.summary: Some networks use a different kind of envelope. This says how to put Internet packets inside it so they get delivered.

questions: how does ip run over novell ipx
what is the mtu for ip over ipx
subtitle: How to carry IP, ARP and other 802.2 traffic over Novell IPX networks, including through IPX bridges.

tldr.problem: Hosts on IPX networks need a standard way to carry Internet packets, and the earlier documents handled only IP and did not cover IPX bridges.
tldr.mechanism: IEEE 802.2 packets are put inside IPX datagrams, so IPX acts as another 802.X physical layer. ARP maps IP addresses to a 10-byte address made of the IPX network and node.
tldr.outcome: It obsoletes the earlier documents and lets several network protocols share IPX. The MTU is 538 bytes.

today: RFC 1132 is an Internet Standard and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Purpose and Approach
sections.content:
RFC 1132 aims at interoperable transmission of Internet packets such as IP, ARP and CLNP over IPX networks. IPX is a proprietary Novell protocol derived from Xerox's Internet Datagram Protocol. The RFC defines the encapsulation of IEEE 802.2 over IPX, which lets IP datagrams be sent as described in RFC 1042.

It obsoletes earlier documents on Internet packets over IPX. It differs from them by allowing several network protocols over IPX and by allowing packets to cross IPX bridges.
sections.eli5: Instead of making one rule for each kind of mail, it makes one rule that any 802.2 mail can use.

sections.title: Addresses and Byte Order
sections.content:
IP addresses are mapped to 802.IPX addresses with the Address Resolution Protocol, as for other IEEE 802.X addresses. An 802.IPX physical address is 10 bytes: the 4 bytes of the IPX network address followed by the 6 bytes of the IPX node address.

Bytes go on the wire in "big-endian" order. The IPX socket 0x8060 is reserved by Novell for this protocol, and as with most IPX applications the IPX checksum is not used.
sections.eli5: An address here has two parts, which network and which computer, glued together. Bytes are sent biggest end first.

sections.title: Broadcast, Unicast and MTU
sections.content:
To broadcast, set the IPX Packet Type to 0x14, the Destination Network to the local network number, the Destination Node to 0xffffff, and the Immediate Address in the IPX Event Control Block to 0xffffff. To unicast, set Packet Type to 0x04, use the network and node found by address resolution, and set the Immediate Address to the destination's physical address or the appropriate IPX bridge.

An IPX datagram carries at most 546 bytes. The 802.2 LLC and SNAP headers take 8 bytes, so the MTU is 538 bytes.
sections.eli5: Shouting to everyone and talking to one friend use different settings on the envelope. The envelope holds a limited amount, so messages stay small.

sections.title: Implementation Notes
sections.content:
A typical IP over IPX packet has a physical header, a 30-byte IPX header, an 8-byte 802.2 header, usually a 20-byte IP header, usually a 20-byte TCP header, and up to 498 bytes of TCP data. On workstations that already have an IPX programming interface, the only change the author describes was widening ARP cache entries so they can hold the immediate address of a possible bridge.

For systems without an IPX interface, such as a dedicated router, the RFC notes that no unicast packet is sent from one host to another without a prior broadcast from the other, so the bridge's immediate address can be learned from that broadcast's physical header. It also says the memo does not address security.
sections.eli5: The packet is a stack of labelled layers. A host learns the relay's address from the first shout it hears.
